newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says January money levels below ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Manila says January money levels below ceiling.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Wednesday that base and reserve money levels were 30 billion pesos below the ceiling set by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

"(Central Bank's) operating targets of base money and reserve money were kept significantly below programme ceilings supported by the International Monetary Fund," the Central Bank said in a statement.
It did not disclose the actual levels of the base money and reserve money.
Base money includes money in circulation, reserve balances and government securities deposited with the central bank and the aggregate reserve deficiencies of banks.
Reserve money is base money minus the government securities deposited with the central bank.
Growth in domestic liquidity slowed to 16.7 percent in November from its peak of 45.4 percent in April 1995.
Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson attributed the tighter monetary situation to a decelerating inflation rate. Nationwide inflation slowed to 5.0 percent in January from 5.2 percent in December.
"With the peso-dollar rate and interest rates also stable, financial variables have been generally indicative of decelerating inflation," he said.
He said average inflation could be brought down between 6.0 and 7.0 percent this year from 8.4 percent in 1996.
